criteria.title: Non-text Content
criteria.what: All non-text content presented to the user has a text alternative that serves the equivalent purpose, except for decorative content, controls, and a defined set of exceptions.
criteria.how_to_meet: Every , , and needs an accessible name. Use the alt attribute for images. Decorative images get alt="" (empty, not missing). Functional images (icons used as buttons) describe the action, not the icon. SVGs need a child or aria-label. CSS background images conveying meaning must have a text equivalent. <canvas> and <object> need fallback content.
criteria.common_failures: Missing alt attribute on ; alt="image" or filename as alt text; decorative icon-fonts without aria-hidden="true"; SVG without ; <input type="image"> without alt.

criteria.title: Audio-only and Video-only (Prerecorded)
criteria.what: Prerecorded audio-only content has a transcript; prerecorded video-only content has a transcript or audio description.
criteria.how_to_meet: Provide a text transcript adjacent to the media or via a clearly labelled link. For silent video showing important visual information, either describe the events in text or supply an audio track narrating them.
criteria.common_failures: Embedded podcast without transcript; silent demo videos without described content.

criteria.title: Info and Relationships
criteria.what: Information, structure, and relationships conveyed through presentation can be programmatically determined or are available in text.
criteria.how_to_meet: Use semantic HTML: headings (<h1>-<h6>) for sections, <label> for form controls, <th> + scope for table headers, <fieldset>/<legend> for grouped inputs, <ul>/<ol> for lists. ARIA can paper over gaps but native semantics first. Don't fake headings with bold text or fake lists with dashes.
criteria.common_failures: Form input without an associated

criteria.title: Meaningful Sequence
criteria.what: When the sequence of content affects its meaning, a correct reading sequence can be programmatically determined.
criteria.how_to_meet: DOM order should match visual order. Don't reorder with CSS in a way that breaks logical reading. Avoid positive tabindex values that fight the DOM order.
criteria.common_failures: CSS grid/flex reorder that puts the call-to-action before its label in DOM; tabindex="1" on random elements.

criteria.title: Orientation
criteria.what: Content does not restrict its view and operation to a single display orientation, unless a specific orientation is essential.
criteria.how_to_meet: Don't lock orientation via CSS @media (orientation) or JS unless the task genuinely requires it (e.g. a piano keyboard demo).
criteria.common_failures: Mobile site that breaks in landscape; viewport meta with user-scalable=no combined with orientation lock.

criteria.title: Identify Input Purpose
criteria.what: The purpose of each input field collecting information about the user can be programmatically determined.
criteria.how_to_meet: Use the HTML autocomplete attribute with the appropriate token (name, email, tel, street-address, etc.) on inputs collecting personal information. This helps password managers and assistive tech autofill consistently.
criteria.common_failures: Login form without autocomplete="username" / "current-password"; address form without autocomplete on street-address etc.

criteria.title: Use of Color
criteria.what: Colour is not used as the only visual means of conveying information, indicating an action, prompting a response, or distinguishing a visual element.
criteria.how_to_meet: Pair colour with shape, text, or pattern. Required fields get a text indicator ("required") not just a red asterisk colour. Validation errors include an icon and message, not just red borders. Links inside body text need a non-colour cue (underline, weight, or icon).
criteria.common_failures: Pie chart legend keyed by colour only; "items in red are sold out" with no other cue; links distinguished from body text only by colour.

criteria.title: Contrast (Minimum)
criteria.what: The visual presentation of text and images of text has a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1, except for large text (3:1), incidental text, and logotypes.
criteria.how_to_meet: Use a contrast checker on every text/background pair. Body text targets 4.5:1 against its background. Large text (18pt or 14pt bold) targets 3:1. Light grey on white is the common offender; bump body text to at least #595959 on white.
criteria.common_failures: Placeholder text in form inputs that's too light; muted helper text on white; brand colours on coloured backgrounds without a contrast check.

criteria.title: Resize Text
criteria.what: Except for captions and images of text, text can be resized without assistive technology up to 200 percent without loss of content or functionality.
criteria.how_to_meet: Use relative units (rem, em, %, vw) for text. Avoid fixed px containers that clip when text grows. Test by zooming to 200% in the browser.
criteria.common_failures: Fixed-height nav bar that clips at 200% zoom; text in fixed-width tooltips truncated when scaled.

criteria.title: Reflow
criteria.what: Content can be presented without loss of information or functionality, and without requiring scrolling in two dimensions, at a viewport of 320 CSS pixels wide.
criteria.how_to_meet: Build responsive layouts. At 320px viewport width, content shouldn't overflow horizontally. Tables and code blocks are the usual exceptions and may scroll.
criteria.common_failures: Fixed-width 1200px container; multi-column layout that doesn't collapse; modal that overflows on mobile.

criteria.title: Non-text Contrast
criteria.what: The visual presentation of UI components and graphical objects has a contrast ratio of at least 3:1 against adjacent colours.
criteria.how_to_meet: Button borders, form input borders, focus indicators, and icons that convey state need 3:1 contrast with the surrounding background. Don't rely on a 1px light-grey input border on white.
criteria.common_failures: Form inputs with #ddd border on white; outline-only buttons in light brand colour on white; focus rings in pale blue.

criteria.title: Text Spacing
criteria.what: No loss of content or functionality occurs when users override text spacing properties.
criteria.how_to_meet: Allow line-height up to 1.5x font size, paragraph spacing 2x, letter-spacing 0.12em, word-spacing 0.16em — without text being clipped or overlapping. Avoid fixed heights on text containers.
criteria.common_failures: Buttons with fixed height that clip taller text; cards with overflow:hidden that hide expanded line-heights.

criteria.title: Keyboard
criteria.what: All functionality of the content is operable through a keyboard interface without requiring specific timings for individual keystrokes.
criteria.how_to_meet: Every interactive element must work via Tab/Enter/Space/arrows. Use native <button>, <a>, <input>. If you build a custom widget, add role + keyboard handlers (Enter and Space for buttons, arrow keys for menus/tabs/grids). Mouse-only interactions (drag without keyboard alternative, hover-only menus) violate this.
criteria.common_failures: <div onClick> without role+tabindex+keypress handler; hover-only dropdown menu; drag-to-reorder without keyboard equivalent.

criteria.title: No Keyboard Trap
criteria.what: If keyboard focus can be moved to a component, it can be moved away from that component using only the keyboard.
criteria.how_to_meet: Modal dialogs trap focus inside but Escape closes them. Embedded video players must allow Tab to escape. Don't suppress Tab globally.
criteria.common_failures: Modal that catches Tab forever; embedded iframe player that consumes all keys.

criteria.title: Bypass Blocks
criteria.what: A mechanism is available to bypass blocks of content that are repeated on multiple pages.
criteria.how_to_meet: Provide a 'Skip to main content' link as the first focusable element. Use landmarks (<header>, <nav>, <main>, <footer>) so screen reader users can jump between regions.
criteria.common_failures: No skip link; same nav repeated on every page with no way past; only landmark is <main>, no <nav> or <header>.

criteria.title: Page Titled
criteria.what: Web pages have titles that describe the topic or purpose.
criteria.how_to_meet: Every page has a <title> describing its content. SPAs update document.title on route change.
criteria.common_failures: <title> missing; same title on every page of an SPA; title says only "App" or the brand name.

criteria.title: Focus Order
criteria.what: If a Web page can be navigated sequentially and the sequences affect meaning, focusable components receive focus in an order that preserves meaning.
criteria.how_to_meet: Avoid positive tabindex. Visual order should match DOM order. When inserting modals or off-screen panels, manage focus explicitly so Tab order doesn't leap to the end of the DOM.
criteria.common_failures: tabindex="1", "2" sprinkled around; floated sidebar that comes first in DOM but appears last visually; opened modal where focus is still on the trigger underneath.

criteria.title: Link Purpose (In Context)
criteria.what: The purpose of each link can be determined from the link text alone or from the link text together with its programmatically determined context.
criteria.how_to_meet: Link text describes the destination: 'Read the docs' not 'click here'. For icon-only links, use aria-label. Adjacent text counts as context, but identical link text pointing at different URLs is a fail.
criteria.common_failures: <a> with no text content (icon-only without aria-label); 'Click here' / 'Read more' as link text; identical 'Read more' on multiple cards.

criteria.title: Headings and Labels
criteria.what: Headings and labels describe topic or purpose.
criteria.how_to_meet: Heading text describes the section that follows. Form labels describe what the input collects. Don't reuse the same heading text for different sections.
criteria.common_failures: Multiple 'Details' headings on one page; labels that say only 'Field 1', 'Field 2'.

criteria.title: Focus Visible
criteria.what: Any keyboard operable user interface has a mode of operation where the keyboard focus indicator is visible.
criteria.how_to_meet: Don't remove the focus outline without replacing it. Use :focus-visible to style focus only for keyboard users. The replacement must have 3:1 contrast with surroundings.
criteria.common_failures: Global * { outline: none } in CSS; focus ring removed on buttons because designers think it's ugly.

criteria.title: Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)
criteria.what: When a user interface component receives keyboard focus, the component is not entirely hidden due to author-created content.
criteria.how_to_meet: Sticky headers/footers must not entirely cover the focused element. When focus moves into an element below a sticky header, scroll-margin or scroll-padding should reveal it.
criteria.common_failures: Sticky header that hides the focused form input; cookie banner covering the bottom focused button.

criteria.title: Label in Name
criteria.what: For user interface components with labels that include text or images of text, the accessible name contains the text that is presented visually.
criteria.how_to_meet: If a button visually reads 'Save', the accessible name (aria-label, alt, or text content) must include 'Save'. Don't aria-label a 'Save' button as 'Submit form'.
criteria.common_failures: aria-label that overrides visible text with synonyms; icon button with aria-label that doesn't match the visible tooltip.

criteria.title: Target Size (Enhanced)
criteria.what: The size of the target for pointer inputs is at least 44 by 44 CSS pixels.
criteria.how_to_meet: Buttons, links, and form controls have a 44x44px hit area on touch devices. Inline links can be smaller if there's an alternative path.
criteria.common_failures: Tiny close-X icons on toasts; navigation links 20px tall on mobile.

criteria.title: Target Size (Minimum)
criteria.what: The size of the target for pointer inputs is at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels, except where exceptions apply.
criteria.how_to_meet: Interactive controls have a 24x24px minimum target, or there's sufficient spacing between adjacent targets, or the target is inline in a sentence.
criteria.common_failures: Adjacent 16px icon buttons in a toolbar; tiny tap-to-dismiss areas.

criteria.title: Language of Page
criteria.what: The default human language of each Web page can be programmatically determined.
criteria.how_to_meet: Set lang on the root <html> element: <html lang="en-GB">. Screen readers use this to pick the right voice and pronunciation.
criteria.common_failures: <html> without lang; lang="en" on a page that's actually French; SPA where the lang attribute never updates.

criteria.title: Language of Parts
criteria.what: The human language of each passage or phrase in the content can be programmatically determined.
criteria.how_to_meet: When a span of text switches language, wrap it in …. Required for quoted text and inline foreign phrases.
criteria.common_failures: Translated quote without lang on the surrounding element.

criteria.title: On Input
criteria.what: Changing the setting of a UI component does not automatically cause a change of context unless the user has been advised of the behaviour before using the component.
criteria.how_to_meet: Selecting from a <select> shouldn't auto-submit the form or navigate. Use a submit button. If auto-submit is needed, warn the user.
criteria.common_failures: Country dropdown that submits on change; sort dropdown that navigates immediately.

criteria.title: Error Identification
criteria.what: If an input error is automatically detected, the item that is in error is identified and the error is described to the user in text.
criteria.how_to_meet: Tie error messages to the input via aria-describedby. Use aria-invalid="true" on the offending field. Don't communicate errors only with red borders.
criteria.common_failures: Toast notification only; red border with no text message; error message far from the input.

criteria.title: Labels or Instructions
criteria.what: Labels or instructions are provided when content requires user input.
criteria.how_to_meet: Every input has a <label> or aria-label/aria-labelledby. Placeholder text is not a label. If a field has format requirements (e.g. date format), say so.
criteria.common_failures: <input> with only a placeholder; search field with magnifying-glass icon and no label; password field without strength requirements stated.

criteria.title: Accessible Authentication (Minimum)
criteria.what: A cognitive function test (such as remembering a password or solving a puzzle) is not required for any step in an authentication process, unless that step provides an alternative or assistance.
criteria.how_to_meet: Allow paste into password fields (don't block paste). Support password managers (autocomplete="current-password"). Offer passkeys or magic-link as an alternative to CAPTCHAs and security questions.
criteria.common_failures: Disabling paste in password fields; CAPTCHA without an audio or cognitive alternative.

criteria.title: Parsing (obsolete in WCAG 2.2)
criteria.what: Obsolete: WCAG 2.2 removed this SC because HTML parsers recover from the kinds of errors it targeted. Kept here for reference; axe-core has dropped its parsing rules.
criteria.how_to_meet: Still write valid HTML — duplicate IDs and unclosed tags cause real issues even if the SC is obsolete.
criteria.common_failures: Duplicate id values; mismatched ARIA references.

criteria.title: Name, Role, Value
criteria.what: For all UI components, the name and role can be programmatically determined; states, properties, and values that can be set by the user can be programmatically set; and notification of changes is available.
criteria.how_to_meet: Custom controls expose role, name, and value. Native HTML gets this for free; use it. If you build a custom toggle, use role="switch" + aria-checked. <button> without text needs aria-label. <iframe> needs a title.
criteria.common_failures: <button></button> with no accessible name; <select> with no <option> labels; <iframe> without title; <input type="image"> without alt.

criteria.title: Status Messages
criteria.what: Status messages can be programmatically determined through role or properties such that they can be presented to the user by assistive technologies without receiving focus.
criteria.how_to_meet: Use aria-live="polite" for non-urgent updates (saved, error appeared) and aria-live="assertive" for urgent (validation blocking submit). Or use role="status" / role="alert". The live region must exist in the DOM before content is inserted, otherwise it won't announce.
criteria.common_failures: Toast appears with no aria-live; cart counter updates silently; validation summary appears but isn't announced.
